title: Dimension devissage for commuting ell-adic representations

source.place: Paragraph (3), dense-lattice analytic input; agent expansion, returned comparison proof step 6: strong dimension induction through kernels of commuting generator differences. Agent-formulated extraction; not asserted to be a theorem stated in the blueprint.

proof.text: Use the already proved Representation.continuousCoefficient_subquotients (lem-sfb-continuous-representation-subquotients) to obtain, for any stable submodule, the induced continuous actions on it and its actual quotient, with equivariant subtype and quotient maps. No choice of a vector-space model is needed.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion: commuting-representation dimension induction, step 1

proof.text: Apply strong induction to the finite dimension, simultaneously for every coefficient representation on every space in the given universe. First discharge the case of an invertible generator difference using hypothesis (ii).

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion: commuting-representation dimension induction, step 2

proof.text: If every generator difference vanishes, every standard generator acts as the identity. For one coordinate, integer multiples of the generator act trivially by the homomorphism power law. PadicInt.denseRange_intCast and the closed equalizer of the continuous orbit map with the constant vector then show every p-adic multiple acts trivially. Pi.single_induction decomposes any finite tuple as a sum of its single-coordinate tuples, so the entire lattice acts trivially. Hypothesis (i) applies. This includes rank zero and the zero vector space.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion: commuting-representation dimension induction, step 3

proof.text: In the remaining case choose a nonzero singular generator difference A. Set U = ker A. LinearMap.isUnit_iff_ker_eq_bot proves U is nonzero, and nonzeroness of A proves U is proper. For every g, commutativity of the lattice gives T_i rho(g) v = rho(g) T_i v, so U is stable under the action.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion: commuting-representation dimension induction, step 4

proof.text: Submodule.finrank_lt gives dim U < dim V from properness. Nonzeroness of U gives dim U > 0 using Submodule.finrank_eq_zero, and Submodule.finrank_quotient_add_finrank therefore gives dim(V/U) < dim V. These are direct finite-dimensional Mathlib interfaces; an explicit extended basis is unnecessary.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion: commuting-representation dimension induction, step 5

proof.text: Apply the subquotient interface from step 1 to U. The strong induction hypothesis gives P for each of its two continuous representations, since their dimensions are smaller. Hypothesis (iii), with the supplied equivariant canonical maps, gives P for V. The actual subspace and quotient are used, so equivariant-isomorphism invariance is not required by this proof.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion: commuting-representation dimension induction, step 6
